observer.collector_defect_history: The 2026-09-23 samples failed in the deletion window because the collector rejected list items without a per-item kind field. Commit 22d7298 removed those checks; the label marker and the namespace-scoped Pod read remain fail-closed.
observer.sampling_method: Read-only local loop started before the deletion request and continued past completion. The run was the normal browser workflow; no workflow was started to obtain a sample.

gateway_namespace_pods.note: Deleted by its ReplicaSet between two dense samples; no termination record was observed.

pod_observations.other_allocated_namespaces_pods: The sandbox, gateway-state, and console-state namespaces held no Pods in any sample.

finalizer_observations.metadata_finalizers: None on any owned namespace or observed Pod.
finalizer_observations.namespace_deletion_conditions: The gateway namespace showed NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure=False, NamespaceDeletionGroupVersionParsingFailure=False, NamespaceDeletionContentFailure=False (ContentDeleted), NamespaceContentRemaining=False (ContentRemoved), and NamespaceFinalizersRemaining=False (ContentHasNoFinalizers). No stuck condition or finalizer was observed in any owned namespace.

diagnostic_conclusion: The delay is not caused by a stuck finalizer, remaining content, failed discovery, or a long application retry interval. The owned Pods terminate with exit code 0 within about 5 seconds. The whole cleanup time is the sum of three sequential Kubernetes namespace termination cycles: the gateway namespace (about 13 seconds), then the sandbox namespace (about 8 seconds after its deletion request, which the application issues only after the gateway namespace is absent), then the two state namespaces in parallel (about 8 seconds after their deletion requests, which the application issues only after the sandbox namespace is absent). The application's sequential wait policy compounds these cycles.
change_evaluation: Per the review requirements, a latency change needs fault tests. The observation supports a candidate change in the application's deletion order (requesting the sandbox and state namespace deletions earlier, or waiting in parallel), which is Hypershell domain policy and not a STEGO mechanism change. The 30-second target remains open: the fourth complete 100-account sample has an observed upper bound of 30.77 seconds.
limitations: One workflow observation; not a latency distribution.
Completion checks and observer samples bound the transitions; they are not exact transition times.
Sequential observations read resource state at different times within one sample.
The deleted console Pod was removed between two dense samples; its own termination record was not captured.
Empty Sandbox namespaces do not establish the behavior of running Sandbox workloads.
The collector fix (commit 22d7298) is an observation-tool change; cleanup source, permissions, and barriers are unchanged.
scope: Observation only. No runtime behavior changed.
